title: Applied ML Eval & Regression Playbook: Integrated Guide
author: Alyssa Chen
body:
Summary:
This document describes Redwood's integrated Applied ML evaluation and regression playbook. It unifies guidance for the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and the regression triage process. The playbook is intended for ML engineers, SREs supporting model deployments, and product owners responsible for model quality and cost tradeoffs.

Table of contents:
1) Purpose and scope
2) Roles and ownership
3) Eval harness standards and onboarding
4) Prompt sets and benchmark design
5) Model onboarding checklist
6) Quality guardrails and automated checks
7) Quantization profile integration and validation
8) Regression triage playbook (runbook)
9) Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards
10) Reporting, postmortem, and continuous improvement

1) Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single, repeatable process for evaluating models before serving, detecting regressions post-deploy, and coordinating remediation across teams.
- Scope: Applies to all models considered for Redwood hosted, dedicated, and private deployments including licensed and open-source model variants. This playbook covers unit and end-to-end evals relevant to generation, conversation, embeddings, and reranking workloads.

2) Roles and ownership
- Model Owner (primary): responsible for onboarding, maintaining prompt sets, and triaging quality issues.
- Eval Engineer: implements eval harness jobs, writes automated checks, and maintains CI eval pipelines.
- SRE / Serving Runtime Owner: validates performance (latency, memory, KV behavior) and implements rollout/fallback policies.
- Product / PM Owner: defines user-facing quality thresholds and approves release for production.
- Incident Manager: coordinates regression triage and communicates status to stakeholders.

3) Eval harness standards and onboarding
Intro: Eval harness must be reproducible, parameterized, and runnable both locally and in CI. All harness jobs are versioned alongside model artifacts.
Minimum requirements:
- Harness repo: GH repo with a standardized CLI (e.g., eval-runner) and documented flags for dataset path, seed, model_url, batch_size, and profile.
- Artifacts: test vectors (prompt/expected output pairs), metric calculators, examples, and output serialization (JSONL).
- Reproducibility: fixed RNG seeds, pinned tokenizer/version, and a recorded model commit/hash.
- CI integration: mandatory pre-merge eval job for model-onboarding PRs and daily scheduled regression scans for production models.
- Example CLI: 
  eval-runner --model-url s3://models/redwood/llama-3-small:2026-02-01 --prompt-set test_vectors.jsonl --metrics metrics.yaml --output results.jsonl --seed 42

4) Prompt sets and benchmark design
Guidelines for prompt sets:
- Coverage: include representative inputs for the primary user flows (happy path, edge cases, adversarial probes).
- Size: minimum 500 prompts for general-purpose models; smaller task-specific sets allowed (e.g., 200-300) if documented.
- Labeling: each prompt must include metadata tags: domain, flow, difficulty, expected_behavior, and owner.
- Versioning: prompt sets stored in the prompt-sets catalog with semantic versioning (vMAJOR.MINOR).
- Examples of tags: ["email-drafts", "summarization", "high-verbosity", "safety-check"].
Benchmark composition:
- Unit benchmarks (fast): token-level metrics, perplexity proxies, and small-scale QA/hallucination tests.
- System benchmarks (thorough): multi-turn chat sims, long-context continuation, embedding similarity stability, and end-to-end latency under load.
- Acceptance criteria: defined per customer/product and attached as an artifact to every model onboarding PR.

5) Model onboarding checklist
Before a model can be marked "production-ready", the following must be completed (checklist):
1. Model artifact uploaded with immutable identifier (S3/GCS object + digest).
2. Eval harness run: pass on all required benchmarks with documented results attached.
3. Prompt set assignment: link to canonical prompt-sets entry and owner.
4. Quantization profile assigned (if applicable) and validated on representative workloads.
5. Performance validation: latency P50/P95, memory usage, and KV-cache behavior measured on target infra.
6. Security & compliance review: data access, logging, and privacy compat checked.
7. Rollout plan: canary percentages, rollback markers, and fallback model variants listed.
8. Documentation: integration snippet, example payloads, and known limitations captured in confluence.

6) Quality guardrails and automated checks
Automated checks integrated into CI/CD:
- Unit checks: deterministic tokenization parity, output schema validation (JSON schema checks), and embedding dimensionality checks.
- Quality thresholds: automatic failure if baseline metrics degrade >3% absolute or 10% relative on core task metrics (thresholds configurable per model-family).
- Safety checks: automated classifiers for profanity/toxicity with configurable thresholds and an allowlist/denylist system for sensitive terms.
- Regression detectors: delta-based detectors that compute effect size across recent daily runs; alerts triggered when effect size > 0.5 for key metrics.
- Webhook/Slack integration: failing checks open a ticket in the regression-triage board and ping the model owner and on-call SRE.

7) Quantization profile integration and validation
Overview: Quantization is a primary lever for cost reduction; profiles must be validated for quality and runtime stability.
Quantization profile fields (table):
- profile_name: short id (e.g., q4_0-int8)
- model_family: e.g., Llama-3, Mistral
- target_dtype: e.g., 4bit, 8bit
- expected_speedup: reported P50 latency improvement (documented)
- fallback_policy: model variant to fallback to when profile fails runtime checks
Validation steps:
1. Apply quantization profile to model artifact and run unit evals.
2. Run regression gate: compare core metrics to FP16 baseline; require no >2% absolute degradation on user-critical metrics.
3. Stability tests: run long-context simulations and memory-stress tests on representative GPUs.
4. Deploy as canary with traffic cap (default 1%) and monitor quality and runtime errors for 48 hours.

8) Regression triage playbook (runbook)
Purpose: fast detection and remediation of regressions that affect model quality or user experience.
Trigger conditions (examples):
- Automated eval CI fails on daily scheduled job.
- Production alert: user-facing error rate increases, or core metric drops beyond threshold.
- Customer report indicating a qualitative regression (e.g., hallucinations).
Immediate steps (0-30 minutes):
1. Incident Manager acknowledges and creates a triage ticket with "regression" template.
2. Gather artifacts: model id, commit hash, recent eval results, recent config changes, and recent infra changes.
3. If production-impacting, apply emergency routing: divert traffic to last-known-good model variant and scale-up fallback capacity.
Triage steps (30-180 minutes):
1. Reproduce locally using eval harness and the canonical prompt-set for the failing flow.
2. Run delta analysis across recent model versions: use eval-runner --compare --baseline <good> --candidate <bad> to generate effect-size table.
3. Identify root cause candidates: model change, quantization change, tokenizer change, or serving runtime change.
4. If reproducible and caused by model change, rollback to baseline and open a CR for model owner to diagnose.
5. If caused by runtime/infra, engage SRE and apply mitigations (kernel fallback, increase KV cache size).
Post-triage (day 1-7):
- Postmortem: document timeline, root cause, remediation, and follow-ups.
- Preventive actions: add additional tests to the eval harness, tune quantization profiles, or strengthen prompt-set coverage.

9) Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards
Key metrics to track per model-route:
- Quality metrics: task-specific accuracy/F1, hallucination rate, top-1 semantic similarity (embeddings).
- Latency metrics: P50, P95, P99 for generation and embeddings.
- Cost metrics: tokens per request, GPU token-seconds, and cost-per-1k-requests.
- Reliability: request error rate, model OOMs, model restarts.
SLO examples (default):
- Latency: P95 < 200ms for small models (hosted), P95 < 500ms for large models on Dedicated.
- Quality: no >3% absolute degradation on core task metric month-over-month without a documented release.
Dashboards:
- Per-route quality dashboard with trendlines, rolling-window regressions, and alert overlays.
- Canary dashboard: show canary vs baseline comparisons, per-prompt regressions heatmap, and runtime errors.

10) Reporting, postmortem, and continuous improvement
- Postmortems are required for any regression causing customer-visible impact or a sustained metric degradation >5% for >24h.
- Continuous improvement cadence: monthly eval harness review, quarterly prompt-set review, and ad-hoc updates after a regression.
- Knowledge base: every regression postmortem must include a reproducible test case added to the canonical prompt-set and a follow-up ticket for prevention.

Appendix A: Example JSON config for an eval job
{
  "job_name": "onboarding-eval-llama-3-small",
  "model_url": "s3://models/redwood/llama-3-small:2026-02-01",
  "prompt_set": "s3://prompt-sets/email-drafts-v1.jsonl",
  "metrics": ["accuracy", "hallucination_rate", "avg_tokens"],
  "seed": "42",
  "timeout_minutes": "90"
}

Appendix B: Required artifacts table (text)
- model_artifact_id: immutable string ID
- canonical_prompt_set: link + version
- eval_results: JSONL of outputs + metrics summary
- quantization_profile: name + validation report
- perf_report: P50/P95 latency + memory profile
- rollout_plan: canary %s, rollback marker ID
